CommunityCorpusCompletionGate.Purpose: Keep evidence-review eligibility separate from corpus completion, so incomplete coverage is labeled without discarding retrieved evidence or misrepresenting a discovery query as the unseen corpus. This gate controls completion, representativeness, and broad-ranking claims; the platform-specific community and YouTube rules control acquisition, extraction, deduplication, and evidence grading.
CommunityCorpusCompletionGate.Rule:
Source-appropriate terminal successful access_status values are complete and api_visible_complete. If any principal-community retrieval reports another access_status; extraction_coverage as partial, search-only, ranked, manual, creator-only, or another incomplete class; an unconsumed next_cursor; has_more=true; or an explicit limitation that results are query-bounded or incomplete, label the corpus partial and preserve the exact records, acquired denominator, method, source scope, time or query window, pagination state, and limitations.
Review and synthesize the retrieved records as bounded evidence; never exclude them solely because the corpus is partial. Do not extrapolate their composition, prevalence, direction, rarity, typicality, strength, weakness, or absence to unseen records, and do not use zero query matches as evidence about the unseen corpus. If more retrieval is useful and possible in the current interaction, continue automatically, retaining the already reviewed partial evidence. If broader retrieval is genuinely impossible, partial output alone does not establish an access boundary: preserve the gap, and apply CommunityCorpusAccessBoundaryCompletion when a completion claim depends on that boundary.

YouTube comment retrieval using searchTerms, keywords, search terms, or other query filters is a discovery operation only: it may locate candidate firsthand reports but can never by itself constitute the directional signal corpus. For every material selected video, retrieve the broadest accessible unfiltered top-level comment corpus, then paginate until exhausted or a genuine access boundary is established, retrieve accessible replies, and reconcile expected versus retrieved replies before using the video for directional community-signal classification. Expand to additional material videos or independent discussion pools when platform coverage requires it, and deduplicate unique people x treatment or exposure episodes rather than counting comments as independent outcomes.

Do not invoke search saturation while additional pages, unfiltered comments, replies, material principal videos, or independent community discussion pools remain retrievable. A small or empty result caused by a restrictive query is not evidence that the corpus itself is sparse and cannot support a weak, absent, rare, indeterminate, or no-signal verdict.

Before synthesis record principal_platforms_mapped; acquisition_mode; unfiltered_retrieval_attempted; pagination_exhausted; replies_reconciled; unique_firsthand_people; unique_treatment_episodes; benefit_search_completed; no_effect_search_completed; harm_search_completed; discontinuation_search_completed; independent_discussion_pools_sampled; and final_coverage_state. Record a missing count as unknown, never silently as zero.
The allowed final coverage states are complete / completed-with-access-boundary / partial. Complete requires the applicable accessible corpus and directional searches to be finished; completed-with-access-boundary requires every condition of CommunityCorpusAccessBoundaryCompletion; partial means some usable evidence was retrieved but coverage did not finish or reach a terminal boundary. Partial evidence must be reviewed and may appear in a bounded synthesis with a prominent coverage label; it cannot support a complete, representative, corpus-wide prevalence, or broad-ranking claim.
